findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that AC5 modifies the degrade-verdict builders (_degraded_plan_review_verdict / _degraded_code_review_verdict) to emit input_rejected vs llm_unavailable by exception type, AND that each of the three readers still degrades input_rejected to INDETERMINATE (never a hollow PASS), so the fuel-posse-ball invariant is preserved.
evidence: Plan: 'LLMInputRejectedError instead sets a distinct input_rejected signal, and the three readers ... are updated to read it'

In live code both exceptions share one catch arm and both call _degraded_*_verdict(error=exc), which unconditionally sets coverage.llm_unavailable=True (gate_dispatch.py:334-336 _degraded_code_review_verdict; :203/:220 plan-review path)
All three readers key strictly on llm_unavailable and drive it to INDETERMINATE / an 'llm-unavailable' gap reason (drift_floor.py:212, orchestrator.py:468, adapter.py:114)
errors.py:57 documents LLMInputRejectedError must 'never surface as an outage' but ALSO must 'never be absorbed into an empty clean result' (fuel-posse-ball)
findings.finding: AC5's mechanism is under-specified where it matters: it must both (a) modify the degrade-verdict builders that emit the boolean, and (b) preserve degrade-to-INDETERMINATE for the new input_rejected signal — otherwise the gates regress to a hollow PASS.
scenarios: A mid-run LLMInputRejectedError sets input_rejected=True; a reader updated to branch only on llm_unavailable no longer degrades, so the gate emits a signed PASS with no findings — the exact hollow-clean-result invariant the type was created to prevent

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify, co-located with the new `input_rejected` signal, the verdict it must drive (e.g. INDETERMINATE, matching today's llm_unavailable behavior) and add the corresponding branch to `finalize_verdict` (orchestrator.py) and `_recompute_verdict_after_drop` (drift_floor.py) so the signal split does not regress a degrade into a hollow PASS.
evidence: AC5: 'LLMInputRejectedError instead sets a distinct input_rejected signal, and the three readers (plan_review/drift_floor.py, plan_review/orchestrator.py, review_bot/adapter.py) are updated to read it' — but never states the resulting VERDICT.
orchestrator.py:459-469 finalize_verdict derives INDETERMINATE only via `coverage.get('llm_unavailable')` (and prerequisite_indeterminate/config_fault); it has no `input_rejected` branch.
drift_floor.py:212 _recompute_verdict_after_drop downgrades BLOCK→INDETERMINATE only `if cov.get('llm_unavailable')`.

Today LLMInputRejectedError is caught in the SAME arm as LLMUnavailableError (gate_dispatch.py:203, 560) and flows to _degraded_plan_review_verdict which sets `llm_unavailable=True` (plan_review_recovery.py:462), yielding INDETERMINATE. Renaming the signal without adding an input_rejected decision branch removes that trigger.
findings.finding: AC5 introduces a new coverage signal `input_rejected` (splitting LLMInputRejectedError off from `llm_unavailable`) but never specifies the verdict/decision rule that signal must drive, so the finalize decision loses its INDETERMINATE trigger for this failure and could fall through to PASS.
scenarios: A plan-review run whose prompt is rejected as oversized (LLMInputRejectedError) after the split: the verdict-string derivation sees no `llm_unavailable`, no `input_rejected` branch, and finalizes to PASS instead of INDETERMINATE — an unsigned degrade silently becomes a hollow pass.
A BLOCK verdict whose sole blocking finding the drift floor drops: _recompute_verdict_after_drop no longer sees llm_unavailable and downgrades to PASS.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC5 to state that `input_rejected` degrades to the same unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict as `llm_unavailable` today (never PASS), and that finalize_verdict / _recompute_verdict_after_drop gain an explicit `elif coverage.get('input_rejected')` INDETERMINATE branch alongside the existing `llm_unavailable` branch — not merely 'read it' in the three enumerated readers.
